extracted.intended_audience: readers of history journalism and media criticism (history/news-interested general public)
extracted.subtask_description: An opinion/news commentary evaluating an author's and publisher's responses to documented instances of borrowing/plagiarism in previously published books, focusing on promises to correct, publisher actions, and accountability. The page discusses expectations of timely corrections, acknowledgments, and publisher coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge when borrowings constitute plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should concede when their borrowings from other authors constitute plagiarism, even if the source was cited in footnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text basis: 'attacking Doris Kearns Goodwin for failing to concede that her much-publicized borrowings from author Lynne McTaggart constituted plagiarism, even though Goodwin had cited McTaggart in footnotes...' The expectation is explicit admission when crossing the line from acceptable citation to improper borrowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apologize when mischaracterizing others
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers/critics should correct the record and apologize if they have misrepresented someone's actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text basis: 'I have misrepresented Ms. Goodwin's actions, and I owe her an apology.' Guidance: own mistakes publicly and promptly, as part of fair critique and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow through on promised corrections promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: If an author or publisher promises to correct faulty or plagiarized text, the corrected edition should be produced without undue delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text basis: 'Goodwin was really, really craven for saying she was going to correct her faulty text and then... not doing it!' and 'Four springs have come and gone since Goodwin promised the corrected paperback edition. None has appeared.' Timeliness is emphasized; repeated promises with no action are unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers must pull and correct copies as promised
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers who say they will pull affected copies and issue corrected editions are expected to do so and to ensure corrected versions replace flawed ones in the marketplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text basis: 'We did pull all our copies as promised.' and later evidence that the promised corrected Simon & Schuster edition was not produced. Guidance: publishers should actually remove erroneous stock and follow through with corrected reprints rather than merely claiming to have done so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure coordination and transparency about reprint rights and editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers and authors should be aware of and communicate about reprint rights (e.g., paperback editions from other houses) to prevent uncorrected versions remaining available unknowingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text basis: 'We weren't aware that other copy [from St. Martin's Press] was out there.' The piece treats such ignorance as implausible and unacceptable. Guidance: parties should track and disclose which editions are in print and who holds rights so corrections reach all formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge documented plagiarisms across works
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should acknowledge well-documented instances of plagiarism in any of their works, not just the single work under immediate scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text basis: 'Goodwin has refused to acknowledge the plagiarisms in another book, No Ordinary Time, even though these were well-documented...' Guidance: accountability should extend to all implicated titles when credible documentation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critics/reviewers should not dismiss plagiarism issues relevant to a work's evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary critics and profile writers should treat plagiarism allegations seriously when they bear on an author's body of work rather than brushing them aside as boring or irrelevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text basis: criticism of Thomas Mallon for being 'bored with the topic of plagiarism, and he dismisses it pretty quickly.' Guidance: refusing to engage with relevant ethical issues undermines critical credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accountability is required beyond media-driven corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections and acknowledgments should not occur only under media pressure; ethical responses should be proactive and sustained rather than reactive to publicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text basis: 'correcting her faulty text only when bad publicity required it' and the author's rebuke that promises were made only to placate the media. Guidance: genuine accountability involves proactive correction and transparency, not conditional actions driven solely by publicity.
